$comment: Maps Stream Deck actions onto Microsoft Teams meeting controls.
Teams' local third-party API (ws://localhost:8124) was retired on 2026-06-30
under MC1266901 with no replacement, so controls are driven through UI
Automation instead.
Entries here are MERGED OVER the plugin's built-in defaults, so you only need
to include the controls you want to change. Deleting this file is safe.
'automationId' values are locale-independent and are the preferred selector.
'activePattern' / 'inactivePattern' match the button's accessible NAME, which
IS localized - translate those to use state icons in another language. A
button's name describes the action it performs, so it is the inverse of the
current state: 'Unmute mic' means you are currently muted.
'menu' opens a flyout before looking for the item; 'submenu' opens one more
level inside it. '{arg}' in a menu item selector is replaced by the value the
key is configured with, which is how one translate control covers every
language.
'requiresRole' limits a control to a PowerPoint Live role, 'presenter' or
'attendee', so a key for the wrong role reports itself unavailable.
'stateFromSelection' reads state from UI Automation's selection rather than
from a label, which the drawing tools expose and which needs no translating.
'menuItemToggleAutomationId' is the id the same entry takes in its opposite
state, for menus Teams swaps rather than checks (Hide/Show presenter view).
NOTE: 'ppt-take-control' changes your ROLE. A successful press turns an
attendee into the presenter, so that key retires and every 'presenter' key
below becomes available. The sidecar re-reads state shortly after any press
so the keys follow the change.
Captured from Teams 26255.500.5120.7530 on 2026-09-14, PowerPoint Live added
2026-09-17. After a Teams update, run bin/sidecar/TeamsBridge.exe from a
terminal and send it {"id":1,"cmd":"discover","menu":""} to dump the live
UI tree, then correct the ids below and restart the plugin.
How a shared deck is recognized.
ROLE comes from the meeting toolbar, not from the slide-show root's CSS
class. Only one of the two marker buttons can exist at a time, so they
are authoritative. The class LOOKS like the answer and is not: it tracks
the current view mode, and flips to the attendee value when a presenter
hides their own notes and thumbnails. The class patterns are kept only
as a fallback for when neither button is offered.
Opening grid view unmounts the whole slide-show subtree, root and all, so
the overlay is tracked separately; the toolbar markers survive it too.
$comment2: INK COLOR is read from a drawing tool's accessible name, which looks
like "Pen: Light blue, Thickness 3" - except while that tool's own
flyout is open, because opening it unmounts the tool button and takes
the name with it. For that window the color comes from the flyout's
swatches instead, which is what lets a key recolor on the click
rather than when the flyout closes.
The swatches carry no automation id, so they are matched by name.
This is the union of all three palettes, which differ: the pen has
dark and magenta shades, the highlighter has the 'Faded' ones and
Yellow, and the laser offers only six.
'the selected radio button' is not enough on its own: the pen's
flyout also holds the laser pointer's arrow options and one of those
always reports itself selected, so they are excluded by pattern.
Both lists are localized, like the names they match.

$comment: Teams asks 'Stop presenting?' before ending a presentation, and
the key answers that dialog when it is held down. The dialog's
buttons carry no automationId, so this is the one control matched
by name - which means it is the one control that needs editing if
Teams is not in English. Set 'name' to whatever the confirming
button reads; 'withinClass' keeps the match inside the dialog so
it cannot pick up a toolbar button with the same label.
Captured live 2026-09-18: [Window] 'Stop presenting?'
class='ui-dialog ...' containing [Button] 'Cancel' and
[Button] 'Stop presenting'.
ppt-stop-presenting-confirm.name: Stop presenting

$comment: The label is 'Private view' whichever way it is set, and the button
offers no toggle pattern, so the state lives only in the tooltip.
Chromium publishes that as FullDescription, which reads without
hovering - so stateFromFullDescription matches the patterns below
against it instead of the name.
'Prevent participants from moving...' means private viewing is on;
'Allow participants to move...' means it is off. Localized.
